meta.description: Registry for selection uniqueness, nonuniqueness, degeneracy, and local uniqueness conditions in Phase 3.

selection_uniqueness_classes.meaning: Selection is unique within a bounded local neighborhood or context.
Uniqueness depends on explicit residue, orientation, or admissibility predicates.
Selection is unique only up to a declared equivalence relation.
Multiple candidates are selected, but the set size is formally bounded.
Multiple distinct candidates satisfy the selection metric equally.
All admissible candidates are retained as concurrent process branches.
Selection behavior is intentionally unspecified or probabilistically modeled.
Selection results in an unconstrained number of candidates.

conditions: delta may return multiple admissible candidates
multiple candidates may share equal minimum orientation deviation
degenerate minima require explicit tie handling
local uniqueness holds only when the minimum is strict
branches may collapse to equivalence classes
representative selection is not identical to unique physical continuation
branch equivalence transitivity limits remain explicit
selection may be reconstructable only under strict orientation, residue, and admissibility constraints
observable_projection and delta remain multi-valued targets
